title: Linux platform observation boundary
description: Objective: land the production Linux platform observation/classification surface that task-e87a735386f643fe92c0eeff09bc4275 will later certify. Deliverable: a shared platform contract plus Linux adapter and public runner seam under packages/runner/src/platform/**, with focused tests and the consumer task ID recorded. NOT in scope: claiming execution on Linux, spawning processes, producing conformance/fault evidence, changing doctor output, or weakening Windows behavior. Owned paths: packages/runner/src/platform/** and the minimal @moe/runner root export/surface-test wiring. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/runner test.
definitionOfDone: A frozen, non-empty production boundary vocabulary covers provider launch, Git/workspace and path/symlink observation, locks, signals/cancellation, runtime closure, and crash-recovery observation; tests assert the exact hand-written set and count.
Linux observations classify caller-supplied facts as PROVEN or UNKNOWN with stable reason codes and the PLATFORM_LINUX layer; missing, hostile, stale, or off-host facts never become PROVEN.

The adapter composes existing runner provider, workspace/scope, cancellation, and recovery contracts without copying lifecycle or authority semantics, and contains no child_process/spawn/kill/clock/random environment probing.

@moe/runner exposes a loadable public Linux platform seam, and task-e87a735386f643fe92c0eeff09bc4275 is recorded as the real conformance consumer (task-e94b2055e281489ea9e97820919f6856 consumes only the shared contract, not Linux facts).
pnpm --filter @moe/runner test exits 0 with each refusal test asserting its exact reason code and refusing layer.
taskRails: This is an implementation task, not Linux conformance evidence; completion must say host facts remain UNKNOWN unless actually observed by a later real-host task.
Keep the shared contract OS-neutral and Linux classification separate; macOS cannot inherit Linux facts.
No direct process launch, shell command, wall clock, randomness, or environment probing inside the pure runner adapter.

implementationPlan.description: OS-NEUTRAL CONTRACT. Create packages/runner/src/platform/platform-contract.ts and its one-line sibling platform-contract.js (`export * from "./platform-contract.ts";`). It must contain no OS name anywhere except the `PLATFORM_LINUX` layer member, and no classification logic. Contents: `PLATFORM_OBSERVATION_VERSION = "moe-platform-observation/1"`; frozen hand-written `PLATFORM_BOUNDARIES` with exactly these seven members in this order — PROVIDER_LAUNCH, GIT_WORKSPACE, PATH_SYMLINK, LOCK, SIGNAL_CANCELLATION, RUNTIME_CLOSURE, CRASH_RECOVERY — covering the seven areas DoD 1 names; frozen `PLATFORM_LAYERS` = [PLATFORM_CONTRACT, PLATFORM_LINUX] so a refusal can say whether the OS-neutral shape gate or the Linux classifier answered; frozen `PLATFORM_TRUTH_CLASSES` = [PROVEN, UNKNOWN]; frozen `PLATFORM_ERROR_CODES` = [PLATFORM_BOUNDARY_UNKNOWN, PLATFORM_FACT_MALFORMED, PLATFORM_FACT_ABSENT, PLATFORM_HOST_MISMATCH, PLATFORM_FACT_STALE, PLATFORM_FACT_UNPROVEN, PLATFORM_ARCH_UNSUPPORTED, PLATFORM_CLOSURE_UNPINNABLE, PLATFORM_COVERAGE_INCOMPLETE], each with a `(typeof X)[number]` alias. Types: `PlatformHostIdentity {os, arch, osVersion}` declared here, NOT imported from either provider adapter; `PlatformFailure {ok:false, code, layer, boundary, message}` with factory `platformFailure(code, layer, boundary, message)` returning a frozen object, plus `isPlatformFailure`; `PlatformBoundaryVerdict {boundary, truthClass, failure: PlatformFailure|null}`; `PlatformObservation {observationVersion, host, verdicts, truthClass}`. One OS-neutral gate: `platformBoundaryRejection(boundary, layer)` returning PLATFORM_BOUNDARY_UNKNOWN for a name outside the frozen list, and a `platformHostRejection(host, layer)` shape check built on canonical.ts's `isNormalizedText` — shape only, it must not know what 'linux' means. Comment the WHY on the two-layer split and on why the host identity is declared here rather than imported.

RED SUITE FIRST (TDD). Create packages/runner/src/platform/platform-observation.test.ts against the not-yet-written Linux adapter. Vocabulary tests, deep-equal against hand-written literals rather than length-only checks: `PLATFORM_BOUNDARIES` equals the exact seven-member array AND `.length === 7` AND `Object.isFrozen` is true; same treatment for `PLATFORM_LAYERS`, `PLATFORM_TRUTH_CLASSES` and `PLATFORM_ERROR_CODES` — a list transcribed from the export under test asserts only that it equals itself, so write the literals by hand. Classification tests, every one pinning the exact code AND the refusing layer: (1) a fully coherent linux host with every boundary fact present, fresh and PROVEN yields aggregate truthClass PROVEN and seven PROVEN verdicts; (2) `host.os === "darwin"` yields UNKNOWN for all seven with PLATFORM_HOST_MISMATCH at PLATFORM_LINUX — the assertion that stops macOS inheriting Linux facts; (3) `host.os === "win32"` likewise, which is this repo's actual host; (4) a fact whose own embedded host disagrees with the declared host -> PLATFORM_HOST_MISMATCH; (5) each boundary fact omitted in turn -> PLATFORM_FACT_ABSENT for that boundary only, driven by iterating PLATFORM_BOUNDARIES with an assertion that the generated case count is exactly 7; (6) hostile records — prototype-polluted, extra key, getter that answers differently on a second read, non-normalized text -> PLATFORM_FACT_MALFORMED; (7) a fact whose observedAt is older than `asOf - maxFactAgeMs` -> PLATFORM_FACT_STALE, with a sibling exactly at the boundary that stays PROVEN; (8) a `ProviderRuntimeObservation` with truthClass UNKNOWN -> PLATFORM_FACT_UNPROVEN; (9) an unsupported arch -> PLATFORM_ARCH_UNSUPPORTED; (10) `pinningMethod === "UNSUPPORTED"` -> PLATFORM_CLOSURE_UNPINNABLE on RUNTIME_CLOSURE; (11) an input covering only six boundaries -> PLATFORM_COVERAGE_INCOMPLETE; (12) a boundary name outside the frozen list -> PLATFORM_BOUNDARY_UNKNOWN at layer PLATFORM_CONTRACT, proving the two layers are distinguishable. Aggregate rule: exactly one UNKNOWN verdict forces aggregate UNKNOWN. Closed-vocabulary sweep: collect every code the suite produced into a Set and assert `set.size > 0` AND `set.size === PLATFORM_ERROR_CODES.length`, so a code nobody can reach cannot be added.

LINUX ADAPTER — make it green. Create packages/runner/src/platform/linux-observation.ts and its one-line .js sibling. Flat filename on purpose: do NOT create platform/linux/, that directory belongs to task-e87a735386f643fe92c0eeff09bc4275. Exports: `PLATFORM_LINUX_LAYER = "PLATFORM_LINUX"`, frozen `LINUX_SUPPORTED_ARCHITECTURES` = [x64, arm64], `ObserveLinuxPlatformInput`, `observeLinuxPlatform(input): PlatformObservation`, and `classifyLinuxBoundary(boundary, fact, context): PlatformBoundaryVerdict`. The input composes existing contracts by TYPE and never re-declares them: providerLaunch as `ProviderRuntimeObservation`, scope as `ScopeObservation`, workspace as `WorkspaceInputManifest`, lock as `MirroredLeaseRecord`, cancellation as `ClaudeReconciliation`, crash as `CrashClassification`, pathSymlink as a contract-declared boundary fact; plus caller-supplied `host: PlatformHostIdentity`, `asOf` and `maxFactAgeMs`. Gate order, and it is load-bearing: host shape -> host.os === 'linux' -> arch supported -> coverage complete -> per-boundary (present -> shape/hostile -> embedded host agrees -> fresh against asOf/maxFactAgeMs -> composed contract's own truth). An off-host input must short-circuit before any per-boundary classification, because a Linux verdict about a win32 fact is meaningless. Aggregate truthClass is AND across all seven: one UNKNOWN makes the whole observation UNKNOWN, and nothing anywhere may raise an UNKNOWN back to PROVEN. Map a provider observation's truthClass onto PLATFORM_TRUTH_CLASSES rather than aliasing it — PROVEN from the provider is a candidate that still has to clear host, arch and freshness. Hard prohibitions from task rail 3, all verifiable by grep on the finished file: no `child_process`, `spawn`, `exec`, `kill`, `Date.now`, `new Date`, `Math.random`, `process.platform`, `process.env`. Freshness compares two caller-supplied canonical timestamps only. Use canonical.ts guards for hostile input; do not import `exactRecord` from supervisor/effect-shape.ts. Keep the file <=250 physical lines by `wc -l`; if it crosses, split the per-boundary classifiers into `platform/linux-boundary.ts` + `.js` — that split is pre-approved, do not trim behaviour to fit.

ROOT SEAM WIRING — the step most likely to go wrong. In packages/runner/src/index.ts add ONE curated named export block in the existing house style (a short `/** ... */` saying why each name is on the seam, then explicit named exports — never `export *` from the platform modules, and do not add a file under surface/). Publish the value exports PLATFORM_BOUNDARIES, PLATFORM_LAYERS, PLATFORM_TRUTH_CLASSES, PLATFORM_ERROR_CODES, PLATFORM_OBSERVATION_VERSION, LINUX_SUPPORTED_ARCHITECTURES, PLATFORM_LINUX_LAYER, platformFailure, isPlatformFailure, observeLinuxPlatform, classifyLinuxBoundary, plus the type closure a consumer needs to narrow a verdict without redeclaring anything: PlatformBoundary, PlatformLayer, PlatformTruthClass, PlatformErrorCode, PlatformHostIdentity, PlatformFailure, PlatformBoundaryVerdict, PlatformObservation, ObserveLinuxPlatformInput. Then update packages/runner/src/index-surface.test.ts: add each new VALUE export to `EXPECTED_EXPORTS` with its correct ExportKind tag (`array` for the frozen lists, `string` for the version and layer literals, `function` for the rest), add the new type names to the type-import block, bump the hard-coded `expect(EXPECTED_EXPORTS.length).toBe(116)` by exactly the number of values added, and update the prose comment that tallies the groups. Type-only exports must NOT be listed — they are not runtime keys and would break the equality assertion from the other side. Transcribe by hand from your module sources, never from the namespace under test; that discipline is the whole point of the file and is stated in its header. DO NOT transcribe `runVerifierProcess`, `createNodeProcessLauncher`, `hermeticVerifierEnvironment`, `VERIFIER_PROCESS_ERROR_CODES`, `VERIFIER_PROCESS_LAYERS` or `MAX_VERIFIER_OUTPUT_BYTES` — those are the in-flight verifier-process task's exports and its owner's edit.

MUTATION DRILL, then regression. Epic rail 6 requires proving each refusal test is still attached to its subject; a green suite hides exactly these defects. One at a time, reverting each before the next: (a) delete the `host.os === "linux"` short-circuit — the darwin AND win32 cases must both go red at PLATFORM_HOST_MISMATCH, not merely stay UNKNOWN by luck; (b) make an absent fact default to PROVEN — the PLATFORM_FACT_ABSENT sweep must go red; (c) change the aggregate rule from AND to 'any PROVEN' — the one-UNKNOWN-forces-UNKNOWN test must go red; (d) remove one member from `PLATFORM_BOUNDARIES` — both the deep-equal literal test and the generated-case-count assertion must go red, proving the sweep is not silently producing zero cases; (e) remove one member from `PLATFORM_ERROR_CODES` — the `set.size === length` sweep must go red; (f) make the staleness comparison always return fresh — PLATFORM_FACT_STALE must go red. Record each red. WARNING (shared worktree): another agent's completion hook can sweep your drill edit into a foreign commit, after which `git status` looks clean while the mutation is still live — trust the RED TEST, not git status, and re-run the full suite after reverting all six. Then run `pnpm --filter @moe/runner typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/runner test`. Compare its failures against the step-1 baseline: the only permitted residual red is the foreign namespace assertion from the verifier-process task. Also `wc -l` both new production files and confirm each is <=250 (not PowerShell Measure-Object -Line — it skips blank lines and under-reports).

ADVERSARIAL REVIEW, then commit by explicit pathspec. Read your own diff as an attacker. Is there ANY input where omitting a field yields a better verdict than supplying a malformed one? Can a getter that answers differently on a second read get one value validated and another recorded? Does any code path raise an UNKNOWN verdict back to PROVEN after the fact? Does the shared contract mention any OS other than in the `PLATFORM_LINUX` layer member — grep it for 'linux', 'darwin', 'win32'? Does the adapter contain child_process/spawn/exec/kill/Date.now/new Date/Math.random/process.platform/process.env — grep and prove it does not. Did you create platform/linux/ or platform/macos/ by accident? Then per epic rail 3: `git status --porcelain`, confirm every staged entry is one of YOUR paths, `git restore --staged -- <path>` anything foreign — in particular the six untracked evidence/verifier-process-* files and the modified surface/evidence-surface.ts, which belong to another task — commit with an explicit pathspec listing exactly platform/platform-contract.ts, platform/platform-contract.js, platform/linux-observation.ts, platform/linux-observation.js, platform/platform-observation.test.ts, index.ts and index-surface.test.ts, then `git show --stat` to verify nothing rode along. Completion evidence is the fresh output of `pnpm --filter @moe/runner typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/runner test`, with the foreign namespace-assertion red disclosed verbatim alongside the step-1 baseline showing it pre-existed. State explicitly, per task rail 1, that no Linux host fact was observed by this task and every host fact remains UNKNOWN until a real-host task observes it. Record the consumer edge per global rail Clause 1: task-e87a735386f643fe92c0eeff09bc4275 (Linux effect conformance) is the real consumer of the Linux facts, task-e94b2055e281489ea9e97820919f6856 (macOS effect conformance) consumes only the OS-neutral shared contract and inherits no Linux fact, and this task lands the intra-package edge itself via index.ts and the root namespace test.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
REJECTED: `platform/linux/linux-observation.ts`. Reads natural, plants this task's files inside task-e87a7353's owned path in a shared worktree. Flat `platform/linux-observation.ts` instead; `platform/linux/` is left uncreated for its owner.

REJECTED: a `surface/platform-surface.ts` module. `surface/evidence-surface.ts` is being edited by an in-flight task right now; adding a fourth file there buys nothing. index.ts already publishes four seams as inline curated blocks, so a `/** Platform boundary seam */` block there is house style AND keeps every other new byte inside owned `platform/**`.

REJECTED: importing `PlatformIdentity` from claude-observation.ts (or codex's copy) into the shared contract. Task rail 2 requires the shared contract to be OS-neutral; binding it to one provider adapter's local record is the opposite, and picking between two duplicate declarations would silently bless one. The contract declares `PlatformHostIdentity` and the LINUX adapter does the composing — that separation is the point of the task.

REJECTED: reusing `OBSERVATION_TRUTH_CLASSES` from the Claude adapter for the platform verdict. Same coupling argument. `PLATFORM_TRUTH_CLASSES` is its own two-member list, and the Linux adapter MAPS a provider observation's truthClass onto it — a PROVEN provider fact is still only a candidate, because it must additionally clear the host, arch and freshness gates. Mapping is composition; aliasing would be inheritance of another layer's authority.

REJECTED: reusing `exactRecord` from `supervisor/effect-shape.ts` for hostile-input parsing. It is deliberately unpublished and carries supervisor framing; platform would be importing across areas for a generic guard. `canonical.ts` (`isPlainRecord`, `isNormalizedText`, `isCanonicalUtcTimestamp`, `isHex64`) is the neutral primitive set every area already shares — use it plus a local exact-key check.

REJECTED: an ambient `process.platform` read to decide whether facts are on-host. Task rail 3 forbids environment probing in the pure adapter, and it would make the adapter's answer depend on where the suite runs. The host is a caller-supplied `PlatformHostIdentity` field, which is also what lets a win32 machine test the darwin-host and linux-host paths at all.

REJECTED: a clock read for staleness. Same rail. The caller supplies `asOf` plus `maxFactAgeMs`; the adapter only ever compares two caller-supplied canonical timestamps.

CONSIDERED AND KEPT: aggregate truth is AND, not majority or best-effort. `PlatformObservation.truthClass` is PROVEN only when all seven boundaries are PROVEN. On this win32 host with no real facts every call returns UNKNOWN, which is exactly what task rail 1 requires completion to say.
